title: Kartarpur Sahib

segments.voice: Yesterday, Nankana Sahib, a town mapped by a childhood. Your line was where it began.

A pair of hands, cracked at the knuckles, soil under the nails. A tea glass on a wall at the edge of a field. Somewhere a tractor coughs and goes quiet. In flat farmland near the river Ravi, a white gurdwara rises out of the green, and the fields come almost up to its walls. Yesterday, where Guru Nanak's life began. Today, where it ended, and what he did with the years between: he went home to the soil.
screen: `SOIL UNDER THE NAILS.` → `A WHITE GURDWARA IN THE FIELDS.` → `HOME TO THE SOIL.`

segments.voice: First, the place. Kartarpur, the Creator's town, as year one told. Tradition says Guru Nanak settled here after his long journeys, farmed his own land, gathered a community around hymns, work and a shared kitchen, and died here. Today the gurdwara stands among fields on the Pakistani side of the border, and pilgrims come through the corridor this path met on an earlier day. Second, the hymn. In Raag Sorath, Guru Nanak turns a farmer's work into a picture of the inner life, in paraphrase: make your mind the farmer, good deeds the work, effort the water, and your body the field. Sow the Name as the seed. Let contentment be the plank that levels the soil, and humility the fence around it. It's practical: a farmer can't skip the water or forget the fence, and neither, in the hymn, can a seeker. Third, why it matters that he farmed. After all those roads, the great teacher could have lived on gifts. Tradition says he chose a plow. So when Sikhs speak of earning by honest work, they can point to a field and say, that's where he farmed. Fourth, the end of the story, told briefly because year one told it fully. Tradition says that when he died here, Hindus and Muslims who both loved him laid flowers on either side of him. Today a memorial and a grave stand side by side at Kartarpur. A field, a hymn about a field, and a farmer people of two faiths wouldn't let go.
screen: `THE CREATOR'S TOWN, AMONG FIELDS.` · `MIND THE FARMER, BODY THE FIELD.` · `HE CHOSE A PLOW.` · `A MEMORIAL AND A GRAVE, SIDE BY SIDE.` · then, large: `WHERE HE FARMED.`

segments.voice: See flat green land running to the edge of sight, a white gurdwara in the middle, and a man in plain clothes walking a furrow early, before the heat. Then walk your own field for a minute, the mind as the farmer and the body as the field, and just notice what seed you're sowing today and what fence keeps it safe. If you pray, you can rest on Waheguru.
Kartarpur Sahib. The Creator's town, where tradition says Guru Nanak farmed his own land, gathered a community, and died. Today's word.
Your line: where he farmed. Contentment levels the soil, and humility is the fence. See you tomorrow.
